assertion: The authors estimated these facilities gobble up roughly 82 terawatt-hours of electricity annually... The 82-TWh estimate corresponds to about 2 percent of U.S. electricity.
source_finding: Nature Sustainability: ~82 TWh, ~1.8% of US consumption, ~25.7 Mt CO2
inaccuracy: The article says about 2 percent; the study says about 1.8% of US consumption (2.06% of EIA 2024 retail sales).
sql: SELECT sales_million_kwh FROM energy.eia_electricity_prices WHERE state_abbr='US' AND sector_code='ALL' AND "year"=2024

assertion: Oregon's studied data centers used the equivalent of 18.6 percent of the electricity sold in the state. In Virginia and Iowa, data centers consumed 15.5 and 13.1 percent, respectively.
reason: State shares are in the study's supplementary data, not in the Nature text I could read. Recomputed denominators from EIA: OR 59.68, VA 138.04, IA 54.93 TWh (2024); implied numerators 11.1, 21.4 and 7.2 TWh, together ~40 TWh or half of the 82 TWh national total, which is plausible. Numerators not independently read.
sql: SELECT state_abbr, sales_million_kwh FROM energy.eia_electricity_prices WHERE state_abbr IN ('OR','VA','IA') AND sector_code='ALL' AND "year"=2024
searched: Nature Sustainability hyperscale data centers state shares Oregon 18.6

assertion: Oregon's state data-center share of electricity use grew from about 3 percent in 2015 to about 23 percent in 2025.
source_finding: OPB and ECOnorthwest: ~23% of 2025 retail sales; 14.0 TWh in 2025
reason: 23% recomputed: 14.0 TWh / 61.54 TWh EIA 2025 = 22.7%. The 2015 ~3% is in a slide chart only; the estimates are modeled and preliminary.
sql: SELECT "year", sales_million_kwh FROM energy.eia_electricity_prices WHERE state_abbr='OR' AND sector_code='ALL' AND "year" BETWEEN 2015 AND 2025

assertion: The group estimated that data centers were associated with approximately 96 percent of the state's electricity sales growth between 2020 and 2025.
reason: Neither OPB nor the ECOnorthwest slides state 96%; the full report PDF exceeds the 25MB fetch cap. EIA arithmetic is consistent: OR sales rose 51.02 to 61.54 TWh (+10.53 TWh); 14.0 TWh in 2025 and 'nearly quadrupled since 2020' (KPTV summary) implies about +10 TWh, ~96-97%. Plausible, not read in a primary source.
sql: SELECT "year", sales_million_kwh FROM energy.eia_electricity_prices WHERE state_abbr='OR' AND sector_code='ALL' AND "year" IN (2020,2025)
searched: ECOnorthwest Oregon data centers 96 percent electricity sales growth 2020 2025

assertion: Dominion Energy has estimated that data centers purchased 28 percent of the electricity its Virginia subsidiary sold last year.
source_finding: Dominion 10-K: data centers are 28% (2025) and 26% (2024) of Virginia Power electricity sales

assertion: Because the Harvard study was limited to hyperscale facilities the authors could verify, its electricity-use estimates are likely undercounts (Virginia: about 15 percent versus Dominion's 28 percent).
source_finding: Dominion's 28% is for 2025 and its own territory, all data center types; the study's 15.5% is for 2024 statewide sales
inaccuracy: The article attributes the 15.5% vs 28% gap to undercounting; part of it is mismatched years (2024 vs 2025), geography (Dominion territory vs statewide) and facility scope (all data centers vs verified hyperscale).
sql: SELECT "year", sales_million_kwh FROM energy.eia_electricity_prices WHERE state_abbr='VA' AND sector_code='ALL'
